scope: ONLY exact interface representations that explicitly enumerate every satisfying boundary tuple when boundary arity k is unbounded. For the even-parity boundary relation E_k={x in {0,1}^k : XOR_i x_i=0}, |E_k|=2^(k-1), so any one-record-per-tuple exact table has exponential state size in k. This does NOT block symbolic affine/parity representations, bounded-k interfaces, compressed decision diagrams, or TRACTABLE_ISLAND_CONTRACTION as a whole.

theorem.statement: For every integer k>=1, the even-parity relation E_k on k Boolean variables has exactly 2^(k-1) tuples. Therefore an exact explicit tuple table for E_k has size Omega(2^k) records and cannot satisfy a polynomial-in-k state bound for unbounded k.
proof: There is exactly one value of x_k that makes XOR_i x_i=0, namely x_k = XOR_{i=1}^{k-1} x_i.
Thus projection onto the first k-1 coordinates is a bijection E_k <-> {0,1}^{k-1}.
An explicit tuple-table representation that lists every satisfying tuple needs at least |E_k| records.
Since 2^(k-1) is not bounded by any polynomial in k, unbounded exact parity interfaces defeat a universal polynomial state bound for this representation class.

independent_replay.note: Finite replay is a consistency check, not the proof. The arbitrary-size proof is the bijection above.

authority.source: Beyersdorff et al., On Exponential Lower Bounds for Partially Ordered Resolution, parity construction explicitly uses the 2^(|X|-1) parity assignments; DOI 10.3233/SAT190110.

anti_overclaim: DO_NOT_GENERALIZE_FROM_THIS BARRIER TO THE FULL TRACTABLE_ISLAND_CONTRACTION FAMILY.
FINITE BATTERY REPLAY IS NOT THE ARBITRARY-SIZE PROOF.
